about: SDK 3.0.1: turning sharing off, or deleting what was shared, while an upload is in flight (SPEC.md section 11.7; make_sharing_off.py). Each case is a situation a test builds with a stub server: a recording is being uploaded, the stub HOLDS the request named by `held` (it does not answer), the learner does `action`, and where `then` is `on` turns sharing on again as soon as the call returned. `assert` lists what must hold, each as `key: sentence`. Every case is run `runs` times; a report gives runs passed of `runs` per case.

rules.R1: from the moment the off call returns the SDK hands nothing more to the system and has ended the request that was in flight; what the system had already taken into its send buffer may still go out, which can be the whole segment that was being sent; nothing after it is sent
rules.R2: the off call returns within off_bound_ms even when a request hangs
rules.R3: nothing unsent remains on the device after off or after delete, also after the held request came back
rules.R4: turning sharing on again afterwards works in the same run
rules.R5: a recording made under an earlier consent is never uploaded, whatever happened in between (off and on again in the same run, a kill between off and the delete, a kill between the server's answer to a delete and the device's delete, any number of recordings); it is deleted at the next launch and before every upload pass; and the change of consent is on the device before anything else is done about it

cases.name: put held, off
cases.held_what: a segment PUT to its upload URL
cases.action_what: the learner turns sharing off (the settings switch, setOn(false))
assert: returns_within_bound: the call returns within off_bound_ms and does not throw, although the held request never answers by itself
no_request_after: no start, URL, PUT or take-list request STARTS after the call was made

no_audio_after: at the test's stub, zero bytes of audio arrive after the call returned: neither a PUT that starts after the call was made nor the rest of a PUT that was in flight (a stub that takes nothing before the call sees what the SDK hands over after it; what a real system had already buffered is outside this test and is stated by each SDK)
nothing_unsent_on_device: when the call returns, no unsent recording, segment or state file of the queue is left on the device (on disk, not only in memory)
still_nothing_after_release: the held request is then let go (it answers 200): the queue is still empty and still nothing was sent

cases.name: put held, delete
cases.held_what: a segment PUT to its upload URL
cases.action_what: the learner deletes what they shared (delete), and the server accepts the deletion
assert: returns_within_bound: the call returns within off_bound_ms and does not throw, although the held request never answers by itself
no_request_after: no start, URL, PUT or take-list request STARTS after the call was made

no_audio_after: at the test's stub, zero bytes of audio arrive after the call returned: neither a PUT that starts after the call was made nor the rest of a PUT that was in flight (a stub that takes nothing before the call sees what the SDK hands over after it; what a real system had already buffered is outside this test and is stated by each SDK)
nothing_unsent_on_device: when the call returns, no unsent recording, segment or state file of the queue is left on the device (on disk, not only in memory)
still_nothing_after_release: the held request is then let go (it answers 200): the queue is still empty and still nothing was sent
queue_stopped_before_the_server_is_asked: no upload request starts between the delete call and the server's answer to it
sharing_is_off_after_an_accepted_delete: sharing is off when the call returns, and the learner is not asked again (asking has ended)
on_again_works: the learner turns sharing on with the switch; a recording made after that is uploaded in the same run, under a new contributor

restart_about: R5 (SPEC.md 11.7, contract 1.5.0). `left` recordings wait in the queue, none in flight. From the moment of the call the test makes every deletion of a recording fail (files held open, a storage that refuses, or a switch for tests): what a stop that cannot delete leaves, and what a kill before the deletion leaves. Where `ends` is true the process ends after the call and a new one opens the same storage. `then` is what the learner does next. Each case is run `runs` times.

restart_cases.name: nine left by off, on again
restart_cases.what: the stop cannot delete; sharing is turned on again in the same run while the recordings still cannot be deleted; then deleting works again
assert: returns_within_bound: the call returns within off_bound_ms
earlier_consent_never_uploaded: no start, URL, PUT or take-list request is made for any of the recordings that were in the queue at the call, in any later pass of this process or of a new one
earlier_consent_deleted: they are gone from the device at the next launch, and before the next upload pass, as soon as deleting works again
on_again_works: a recording made after sharing came on again is uploaded, and it is the only one

restart_cases.name: nine left by off, the process ends, sharing off
restart_cases.what: the process ends before the stop deleted anything; at the next launch deleting works and sharing is still off
assert: off_is_on_disk_first: a new process on the same storage finds sharing off: the change of consent was written before the queue was touched
earlier_consent_deleted: they are gone from the device right after the launch, before any upload pass was asked for
earlier_consent_never_uploaded: no start, URL, PUT or take-list request is made for any of the recordings that were in the queue at the call, in any later pass of this process or of a new one

restart_cases.name: nine left by off, the process ends, on again
restart_cases.what: the process ends before the stop deleted anything; at the next launch the learner turns sharing on while the recordings still cannot be deleted; then deleting works again
assert: off_is_on_disk_first: a new process on the same storage finds sharing off: the change of consent was written before the queue was touched
earlier_consent_never_uploaded: no start, URL, PUT or take-list request is made for any of the recordings that were in the queue at the call, in any later pass of this process or of a new one
earlier_consent_deleted: they are gone from the device at the next launch, and before the next upload pass, as soon as deleting works again
on_again_works: a recording made after sharing came on again is uploaded, and it is the only one

restart_cases.name: nine left by an accepted delete, the process ends, on again
restart_cases.what: the server took the deletion and the process ends before the device deleted anything (a kill between the server's answer and the device's delete); the next launch as in the case before
assert: off_is_on_disk_first: a new process on the same storage finds sharing off: the change of consent was written before the queue was touched
earlier_consent_never_uploaded: no start, URL, PUT or take-list request is made for any of the recordings that were in the queue at the call, in any later pass of this process or of a new one
earlier_consent_deleted: they are gone from the device at the next launch, and before the next upload pass, as soon as deleting works again
on_again_works: a recording made after sharing came on again is uploaded, and it is the only one

restart_cases.name: delete, the process ends while the server is asked
restart_cases.what: the process ends while the server is being asked to delete (no answer yet). OPTIONAL: held by an SDK that writes the off to the device before it asks the server and puts the earlier state back when the server did not take the deletion. An SDK that writes the off after the server's answer says so in its report: at its next launch sharing is still on and the queue goes on, which is what a refused deletion leaves
assert: off_is_on_disk_first: a new process on the same storage finds sharing off: the change of consent was written before the queue was touched
